question: Which native drag owner and UI policies should block dragging and drop indicators reuse?
trigger: The user asked whether logic in the copied dnd.tsx should move into a package, and for harsh honest feedback on whether a Plite or Plate API should replace the transfer rules in BaseColumnPlugin, BaseListPlugin, BaseTablePlugin and BaseUploadPlugin.
requirements: A block can be dragged and dropped wherever the schema lets that block live, with one rule shared by drag, keyboard move and custom drivers.
Product limits that the schema cannot express stay with their feature: rows stay in their table and avoid row spans, list items move with their indented family, upload drafts stay in one root.
The copied UI shows a handle only on blocks a block handle can move, without restating plugin types or path depths.
Moves keep the existing laws: no content loss, schema legality at the final edge, inside-source and no-op refusals, read-only targets refuse.
Assessment only: no product implementation in this review.
evidenceReuse: Reused the DnD transfer consolidation plan and its execution record for the transfer pipeline, the landing policy table and the list, column, table and upload rules. Rechecked current source on the working tree: the default transfer.landing read admits only path length 1 (packages/plitejs/src/core/transfer.ts resolveLanding); BaseColumnPlugin and BaseTablePlugin carry the same widening middleware; the copied dnd.tsx restates the depth rule in getDraggableContainer and UNDRAGGABLE_PLUGINS, and payloadOf repeats startDOMDrag in packages/plitejs/src/dom/plugin/dom-drag.ts; blockquote, details and footnote definitions declare block content but get no handle and no drop.
summary: Pursue a schema-derived landing default in Plite. Today the default transfer.landing admits only root blocks, so every container that holds blocks needs feature middleware to take a drop, and the copied dnd.tsx restates the same depths to decide where handles appear. Column and Table each carry near-identical middleware for that, and blockquote, details and footnote definitions, which declare block content, get no handle and no drop at all because nobody wrote theirs. Plite already checks schema legality at the final edge, so the default should admit any edge where the parent content model accepts the payload, and a matching read should say which nodes a block handle can drag. Column and Table then delete their widening middleware; the same-table and row-span rules stay as Table vetoes. List keeps its family source and retarget, which encode flat-list semantics no other feature shares, and Upload keeps its draft veto. The copied dnd.tsx drops its depth policy and payload copy, and keeps the drag image, handle menu and actions. The deferred drag-library comparison in 2026-10-02-dnd-library-choice stands.

reconciliation.question: Which native drag owner and UI policies should block dragging and drop indicators reuse?
reconciliation.reason: Reopens this scope question for landing and handle policy only. Its deferred comparison of the native driver with Pragmatic Drag and Drop stands unchanged and still waits on the integration and production comparison it names.

reconciliation.question: Which native drag owner and UI policies should block dragging and drop indicators reuse?
reconciliation.reason: Its landing policy reproduced the old drop depth exactly; this review replaces the root-only default and the widening middleware with a schema-derived default, keeping its laws, vetoes and list rules.

alternatives: Keep feature middleware: loses. Two near-identical widening rules, a third copy of the depth rule in the copied UI, and blockquote, details and footnote content left without drag for lack of their own middleware; every new block container repeats the work.

Schema-derived default in Plite (selected): admit an edge when the parent content model accepts the payload, which Plite already checks at the final edge, and expose a draggable read from the same content models. Deletes the Column and Table widening middleware and the copied depth policy.
A Plate-level container registry or declarative transfer flag per plugin: loses. It restates content models the schema already holds and adds a second owner for where blocks may live.

Move the copied dnd.tsx logic into a Plate React component: partial. The draggable read and a node option on transfer.move belong in the package; the drag image, handle placement, menu and cut-to-clipboard flow stay copied UI because they are presentation and product choices.
Generalize the List family rule into a flat-outline primitive: rejected for now. No other installed feature has indent families, so it would be a one-caller abstraction.
proofLimits: Source assessment only; nothing was built or run for this review. Whether widening drops into blockquote, details, footnote definitions and content roots keeps every transfer law needs proof per container. The depth limits the old UI had (only root-level column groups and tables) may have been a product choice rather than an accident; no record says either way. Hover dry-pass cost with a schema check on every edge is unmeasured.
